title: SLO-driven request classification and unified retry surface
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem: Services use a mix of ad-hoc retry/timeout/backoff behaviors across call surfaces and SDKs, leading to unpredictable multi-region failover behavior and noisy failover storms during partial outages. This makes SLOs brittle and incr eases operational toil during incidents.

Goal: Provide a single, SLO-driven request classification at the ingress layer that selects from a small set of interoperable retry profiles (and hedging modes), surfaces a clear SDK contract for idempotency, and integrates with circuit-breaker and load-shedding primitives in the runtime. The result should reduce cascading retries, enable predictable failovers across regions, and make SDKs easy to reason about for application teams.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress request classifier tags >95% of traffic into one of three classes (latency-critical, throughput-critical, best-effort) based on headers or route config

Runtime applies correct retry profile for each class with documented defaults: latency-critical -> short single retry with jitter; throughput-critical -> conservative exponential backoff; best-effort -> hedged fanout allowed
SDKs add opt-in idempotency header 'X-RW-IDEMPOTENCY' with scope rules; runtime deduplicates requests within configured time window when present
Circuit-breaker weight respects request class and can trip independently per-class per-region
Load-shedding reduces best-effort traffic first under capacity pressure and produces alerting/metrics in Console dashboards
Integration tests exercise multi-region failover with at least 2 simulated region failures and show <10% additional user-facing errors for latency-critical class
Gradual rollout plan with feature flagging and canary in a single non-prod region documented
Documentation and SDK changelog published; migration guide for teams with non-idempotent operations
notes:
Key design point is decoupling retry semantics from transport-level deadlines. We classify at ingress (API gateway/runtime) and annotate requests; each service/SDK uses the annotation to pick policy. This avoids each SDK independently implementing its own heuristics.

We must balance developer ergonomics: keep SDK defaults safe, but allow opt-in aggressive hedging for workloads that can tolerate duplicates (e.g., search/rerank).
design_decisions: Classification set: 'latency-critical', 'throughput-critical', 'best-effort' to keep surface small and actionable
Four canonical retry profiles: NO_RETRY, FAST_RETRY, BACKOFF_RETRY, HEDGED_FANOUT. Mapping to classes documented in portal

Idempotency header 'X-RW-IDEMPOTENCY' is a client-provided opaque key; runtime applies dedupe if present for BACKOFF_RETRY and NO_RETRY; HEDGED_FANOUT allowed only when caller explicitly opts-in via header 'Prefer-Hedge: true'
Hedged requests spawn at most 2 parallel attempts with server-side coordination to accept first-completing result and cancel others' KV cache effects
Circuit-breakers maintain separate state per request class and region, so best-effort storms don't trip latency-critical paths
Backoff defaults: FAST_RETRY -> 100-300ms +/- jitter up to 2 attempts; BACKOFF_RETRY -> exp backoff starting 200ms, factor 2, max 2s, up to 4 attempts
Load-shedding uses priority token bucket on runtime ingress with reclaimable tokens for latency-critical flows
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Ingress classifier and runtime policy engine (2 weeks). Implement classifier rules and policy table, expose feature flag. Phase 2: SDK changes (3 weeks) — add idempotency header, opt-in hedging API, and convergence tests. Phase 3: Circuit breaker per-class (1 week). Phase 4: Load-shedding & metrics (1 week). Phase 5: Canary rollout + runbook updates (2 weeks).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Canary in region 'us-west-2' for internal services; enable latency-critical/throughput-critical classification only for selected routes. 3) Monitor SLO/latency dashboards for 72 hours. 4) Expand to additional regions with step increases. 5) Flip SDK to use idempotency header by default only for passive clients after 4 weeks of observation.
migration_notes: Teams with non-idempotent write operations must either: a) add an application-level dedupe key and use 'X-RW-IDEMPOTENCY', or b) mark routes as NO_RETRY and accept no duplicate protection. Provide migration script examples and a Confluence playbook. SDKs will provide a helper to generate stable dedupe keys based on request payload+user context.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy selection, dedupe window, and hedged cancellation logic. Integration tests for multi-region failover: simulate increased latency and region fail, assert behavior per class. Chaos job to inject 30% packet loss in a region and verify load-shedding moves best-effort traffic off that region.
metrics_and_alerting: Expose metrics: retry_attempts_by_class, hedged_attempts, dedupe_hits, shed_requests_by_class, cb_open_by_region_class. Create Console dashboards linking these to SLO windows. Alert if retry_attempts_by_class(latency-critical) rises >10% over baseline or cb_open_by_region_class(latency-critical) > 1 for >5m.
risks: Clients may not supply idempotency keys leading to unsafe hedging: mitigate via opt-in and docs
Incorrect classification rules could route critical traffic into best-effort: require route-level overrides and safe defaults
Runtime dedupe window size tuning could cause state bloat: we'll add TTL-based compacting and metrics to track cardinality
recent_updates: 2025-02-20: Spike completed — validated hedged cancellation semantics in local runtime harness. 2025-02-26: SDK prototype for idempotency header implemented; initial integration tests green. 2025-03-03: Performance microbenchmark shows hedged fanout adds ~2% p50 latency for mixed traffic; still within target for best-effort class.
next_steps: Merge runtime policy table scaffolding, open SDK PRs for review, schedule 2-hour cross-functional review with PM/Design/SRE to finalize UX of SDK hedging API. Update runbook to include 'how to opt a route out of classification'
priority_rationale: Reducing cross-region retry storms is directly tied to recent incidents where retries amplified partial regional degradation. This work reduces operational load and protects SLOs for higher-tier customers.
